narration.text: A small firm answers unemployment claim notices from three states by each one's deadline: layoffs and a part-time claim with the facts, a quit and a documented discharge contested with evidence, a stranger's claim and an employee's reported, while a repeat, a late one, a layoff called a quit and a firm's offer to contest all are left alone. This is a chore for the owner of a 24-person surveying firm with remote field staff in Texas, California and Washington, who has ten unemployment notices, one of them only by post, and a field lead who is sure a laid-off man quit. On the bench, she found 7 of 7 eligible items, worth 9,880 dollars of the 9,880 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 8 traps, and she walked past 8. She took 4 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 4 hours, so she was about 53 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
